verdicts.rewritten_summary: UK Home Office country policy and information note on sexual orientation and gender identity for Russia (version 2.0, June 2025; updated 12 August 2026) is the national framework this division is assessed under: same-sex sexual activity is not criminalised, but same-sex marriage and gender transition are banned; the 'gay propaganda' law makes public expression 'promoting' non-heterosexual relationships or gender transition — including displaying rainbow symbols — punishable by fines up to 400,000 rubles (about £3,600) for individuals or detention of up to 15 days, and repeated offences can bring up to four years' imprisonment; trans-specific healthcare was effectively banned in 2023; the Supreme Court designated the international LGBT+ movement an 'extremist' organisation in November 2023, and between 2022 and 2024 at least 139 individuals were impacted by anti-LGBT+ laws. No division-specific information about Bashkortostan appears.

verdicts.rewritten_summary: Human Rights Watch (30 June 2025): Russian courts have issued 101 'extremism'-related convictions for participating in the 'International LGBT Movement' or displaying its symbols since the Supreme Court's November 2023 designation, with penalties of up to 12 years in prison; HRW also identified 81 people in 98 cases found guilty since January 2024 of administrative offences (article 20.3 of the Code of Administrative Offenses) for displaying banned LGBT symbols, mostly on social media; the 2013 'gay propaganda' law already made any positive or neutral depiction of non-heterosexual relations an administrative offence. verdicts.rewritten_summary: BuzzFeed News feature (12 January 2018) on transgender women in French prisons: under Article D248 of the French Criminal Procedure Code men and women are held in separate establishments, so trans women whose legal gender is marked male (the vast majority, without sex-reassignment surgery) are placed in men's facilities; a detainee recalled inmates shouting 'We don't want any women here!' and threats of violence; Adeline Hazan, controller-general of places of deprivation of liberty, says transgender detainees — overwhelmingly women — are the group that suffers the most in prison, illustrated by American trans woman Kara B. held in 'worrying' conditions. National prison-placement framework; no division-specific detail for this region.
verdicts.note: national-framework source; rule-5 retention: record text claims the national framework and no region-specific source exists

verdicts.rewritten_summary: CGLPL (French national preventive mechanism) opinion of 25 May 2021 on the treatment of transgender persons in places of deprivation of liberty (follow-up to its opinion of 30 June 2010): it records the persistence of serious violations of trans detainees' fundamental rights in adult prisons, while none were noted in mental-health establishments, closed educational centres or juvenile detention centres; the review covered the situations of some forty transgender detainees, with interviews including eight trans women and one trans man, and inspection visits at the Fleury-Mérogis, Caen, Saint-Martin-de-Ré and Toulouse-Seysses prisons and the Toulouse central police station. National custodial-inspection framework; no division-specific finding for this region.
